{{About|positive polynomials and positivstellensatz-like theorems|the Krivine–Stengle Positivstellensatz|Krivine–Stengle Positivstellensatz}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''positive polynomial''' (respectively '''non-negative polynomial''') on a particular [[set (mathematics)|set]] is a [[polynomial]] whose values are positive (respectively non-negative) on that set. Precisely, Let <math>p</math> be a polynomial in <math>n</math> variables with [[real number|real]] [[coefficient]]s and let <math>S</math> be a [[subset]] of the <math>n</math>-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>. We say that:
* <math>p</math> is '''positive''' on <math>S</math> if <math>p(x)>0</math> for every <math>x</math> in <math>S</math>.
* <math>p</math> is '''non-negative''' on <math>S</math> if <math>p(x)\ge 0</math> for every <math>x</math> in <math>S</math>.

== Positivstellensatz and nichtnegativstellensatz ==
For certain sets <math>S</math>, there exist algebraic descriptions of all polynomials that are positive (resp. non-negative) on <math>S</math>.  Such a description is a '''positivstellensatz''' (resp. '''nichtnegativstellensatz'''). The importance of Positivstellensatz theorems in computation arises from its ability to transform problems of [[polynomial optimization]] into [[semidefinite programming]] problems, which can be efficiently solved using [[convex optimization]] techniques.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Semidefinite optimization and convex algebraic geometry |date=2013 |others=Grigoriy Blekherman, Pablo A. Parrilo, Rekha R. Thomas |isbn=978-1-61197-228-3 |location=Philadelphia |oclc=809420808}}</ref> In the Hermitian case, Putinar observed that the resulting semidefinite programming problems converge asymptotically and reduce to calculating the largest eigenvalues of explicitly given matrices, which can be solved more efficiently than general semidefinite programming problems.<ref name="n064" />

== Examples ==
===Positive polynomials on Euclidean space===
A real univariate polynomial is non-negative on <math>\mathbb{R}</math> [[if and only if]] it is a [[Polynomial SOS|sum of two squares]] of real univariate ''polynomials''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Benoist|first=Olivier|date=2017|title=Writing Positive Polynomials as Sums of (Few) Squares|journal=EMS Newsletter|language=en|volume=2017-9|issue=105|pages=8–13|doi=10.4171/NEWS/105/4|issn=1027-488X|doi-access=free}}</ref>  This equivalence does not generalize to multivariate polynomials, which was originally shown by Hilbert. An explicit example of such a polynomial was not known until [[Theodore Motzkin]] showed in 1967 that <math>X^4Y^2+X^2Y^4-3X^2Y^2+1</math> is not a sum of squares of polynomials but is non-negative on <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math>, which follows from the [[AM–GM inequality#Motzkin|AM-GM inequality]].<ref>T. S. Motzkin,  The arithmetic-geometric inequality.  1967  Inequalities (Proc. Sympos. Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, 1965)  pp. 205–224.</ref>

In higher dimensions, a real polynomial in <math>n</math> variables is non-negative on <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> if and only if it is a sum of squares of real ''rational'' functions in <math>n</math> variables. This was originally posed as [[Hilbert's seventeenth problem]] in 1900, and later solved by [[Emil Artin]] in 1927.<ref>[[Emil Artin|E. Artin]], Uber die Zerlegung definiter Funktionen in Quadrate, Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg, 5 (1927), 85–99.</ref>

For [[homogeneous polynomial]]s, more information can be determined about the denominator. Suppose that <math>p\in\mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_n]</math> is homogeneous of degree 2''k''. If it is positive on <math>\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}</math>, then there exists an [[integer]] <math>m</math> such that <math>(X_1^2+\cdots+X_n^2)^mp</math> is a sum of squares of homogeneous polynomials of degree <math>m + 2k</math>.<ref>B. Reznick, Uniform denominators in Hilbert's seventeenth problem.  Math. Z.  220  (1995),  no. 1, 75–97.</ref>

=== Positive polynomials on [[polytope]]s ===
For polynomials of degree<math>{}\le 1</math> we have the following variant of [[Farkas lemma]]: If <math>f,g_1,\dots,g_k</math> have degree<math>{}\le 1</math> and <math>f(x)\ge 0</math> for every <math>x\in\mathbb{R}^n</math> satisfying <math>g_1(x)\ge 0,\dots,g_k(x)\ge 0</math>, then there exist non-negative real numbers <math>c_0,c_1,\dots,c_k</math> such that <math>f=c_0+c_1g_1+\cdots+c_kg_k</math>.

For higher degree polynomials on the simplex, [[G. Polya|Pólya]] showed that if <math>p\in\mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_n]</math> is homogeneous and positive on the set <math>\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid x_1\ge 0,\dots,x_n\ge 0,x_1+\cdots+x_n\ne 0\}</math>, then there exists an integer <math>m</math> such that <math>(x_1+\cdots+x_n)^mp</math> has non-negative coefficients.<ref>G. Pólya, Über positive Darstellung von Polynomen Vierteljschr, Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 73 (1928) 141–145, in: [[R. P. Boas]] (Ed.), Collected Papers Vol. 2, MIT Press, Cambridge, MA, 1974, pp. 309–313.</ref>

For higher degree polynomials on general compact polytopes, we have Handelman's theorem:<ref>D. Handelman, Representing polynomials by positive linear functions on compact convex polyhedra.  Pacific J. Math.  132  (1988),  no. 1, 35–62.</ref> If <math>K</math> is a compact polytope in Euclidean <math>d</math>-space, defined by linear inequalities <math>g_i\ge 0</math>, and if <math>f</math> is a polynomial in <math>d</math> variables that is positive on <math>K</math>, then <math>f</math> can be expressed as a linear combination with non-negative coefficients of products of members of <math>\{g_i\}</math>.

===Positive polynomials on [[semialgebraic set]]s===
For general semialgebraic sets, the most general result is [[Stengle's Positivstellensatz]].

For compact semialgebraic sets we have [[Stengle's Positivstellensatz#Schmüdgen's Positivstellensatz|Schmüdgen's positivstellensatz]],<ref>K. Schmüdgen. "The {{mvar|K}}-moment problem for compact semi-algebraic sets".  Math. Ann.  289  (1991),  no. 2, 203–206.</ref><ref>T. Wörmann. "Strikt Positive Polynome in der Semialgebraischen Geometrie", Univ. Dortmund 1998.</ref> [[Stengle's Positivstellensatz#Putinar's Positivstellensatz|Putinar's positivstellensatz]]<ref>M. Putinar, "Positive polynomials on compact semi-algebraic sets". ''Indiana Univ. Math. J.'' 42  (1993),  no. 3, 969–984.</ref><ref>T. Jacobi, "A representation theorem for certain partially ordered commutative rings". ''Math. Z.'' 237  (2001),  no. 2, 259–273.</ref> and Vasilescu's positivstellensatz.<ref>Vasilescu, F.-H. "Spectral measures and moment problems". Spectral analysis and its applications, 173–215, ''Theta Ser. Adv. Math.'', 2, Theta, Bucharest, 2003. See Theorem 1.3.1.</ref> In particular, no denominators are needed.

For sufficiently nice compact semialgebraic sets of low dimension, there exists a nichtnegativstellensatz without denominators.<ref>C. Scheiderer, "Sums of squares of regular functions on real algebraic varieties".  ''Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 352 (2000), no. 3, 1039–1069.</ref><ref>C. Scheiderer, "Sums of squares on real algebraic curves". ''Math. Z.'' 245  (2003), no. 4, 725–760.</ref><ref>C. Scheiderer, "Sums of squares on real algebraic surfaces". ''Manuscripta Math.'' 119  (2006),  no. 4, 395–410.</ref>

===Positive Hermitian polynomials===
A polynomial <math>p</math> in complex variables <math>z_1, \dots, z_n</math> and their conjugates <math>z_1^*, \dots, z_n^*</math> is Hermitian if it takes on only real values for all choices of <math>z</math>. It is a hermitian sum-of-squares (HSOS) if it can be written as <math display="block">p = \sum _{i = 1} ^{k} g_i^*g_i</math> for some polynomials <math>g_1, \dots, g_k</math> in only the variables <math>z_1, \dots, z_n</math>. A result due to [[Daniel Quillen|Quillen]] states that any strictly positive, homogeneous Hermitian polynomial is a Hermitian sum-of-squares of [[Rational function|rational functions]] whose denominator is the squared norm <math>z_1^*z_1 + \dots + z_n^*z_n</math>.<ref>{{cite journal | zbl=0198.35205 | last1=Quillen | first1=Daniel G. | title=On the representation of hermitian forms as sums of squares | journal=Invent. Math. | volume=5 | issue=4 | pages=237–242 | year=1968 | doi=10.1007/bf01389773| bibcode=1968InMat...5..237Q | s2cid=119774934 }}</ref> This was later generalized by Putinar to a much larger class of spaces, including all complex projective varieties.<ref name="n064">{{cite book | last=Putinar | first=Mihai | title=Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry | chapter=Chapter 9: Sums of Hermitian Squares: Old and New | publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics | publication-place=Philadelphia, PA | date=2012 | isbn=978-1-61197-228-3 | doi=10.1137/1.9781611972290.ch9 | url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611972290.ch9 | page=407–446}}</ref> In the Hermitian case the Hermitian sum-of-squares representation is unique if it exists and can be found by diagonalizing an explicitly given [[Hermitian matrix]], which was first observed by Putinar.<ref name="n064" />

== Generalizations of positivstellensatz ==
Positivstellensatz also exist for [[Signomial|signomials]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dressler |first1=Mareike |last2=Murray |first2=Riley |date=2022-12-31 |title=Algebraic Perspectives on Signomial Optimization |url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/21M1462568 |journal=SIAM Journal on Applied Algebra and Geometry |language=en |volume=6 |issue=4 |pages=650–684 |doi=10.1137/21M1462568 |arxiv=2107.00345 |s2cid=235694320 |issn=2470-6566}}</ref> [[trigonometric polynomial]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dumitrescu |first=Bogdan |date=2007 |title=Positivstellensatz for Trigonometric Polynomials and Multidimensional Stability Tests |journal=IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs |volume=54 |issue=4 |pages=353–356 |doi=10.1109/TCSII.2006.890409 |s2cid=38131072 |issn=1558-3791}}</ref> [[Polynomial matrix|polynomial matrices]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cimprič |first=J. |date=2011 |title=Strict positivstellensätze for matrix polynomials with scalar constraints |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |language=en |volume=434 |issue=8 |pages=1879–1883 |doi=10.1016/j.laa.2010.11.046|s2cid=119169153 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1011.4930 }}</ref> polynomials in free variables,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Helton |first1=J. William |last2=Klep |first2=Igor |last3=McCullough |first3=Scott |date=2012 |title=The convex Positivstellensatz in a free algebra |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |language=en |volume=231 |issue=1 |pages=516–534 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2012.04.028 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1102.4859 }}</ref> quantum polynomials,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Klep |first=Igor |date=2004-12-31 |title=The Noncommutative Graded Positivstellensatz |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1081/AGB-120029921 |journal=Communications in Algebra |language=en |volume=32 |issue=5 |pages=2029–2040 |doi=10.1081/AGB-120029921 |s2cid=120795025 |issn=0092-7872|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and definable functions on [[O-minimal structure|o-minimal structures]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Acquistapace |first1=F. |last2=Andradas |first2=C. |last3=Broglia |first3=F. |date=2002-07-01 |title=The Positivstellensatz for definable functions on o-minimal structures |journal=Illinois Journal of Mathematics |volume=46 |issue=3 |doi=10.1215/ijm/1258130979 |s2cid=122451112 |issn=0019-2082|doi-access=free }}</ref>
